title: A cubic lower bound for border determinantal complexity of the permanent
main_claim: For m >= 1408, the complex border determinantal complexity of per_m is at least m^3/(5,529,600 e), so the same holds for exact dc. ABP size is also Omega(m^3). The proof has two halves. (a) Any smooth degree-r form in d variables has bdc >= (r-1)(d-1)/(4e). (b) A coefficient [s^q t^q] per_k(X+sI+tD) has a smooth linear section with r ~ k/3 and d ~ k^2/100, and it is an affine projection of per_{11k-2q}.

issues.description: The char-2 dimension bound for curves with delta >= T rests entirely on an external result: integral plane curves of degree b and geometric genus g form a locus of dimension 3b+g-1 over any algebraically closed field. This includes characteristic 2, with arbitrary singularities. I did not re-verify the cited statement or check that its hypotheses match exactly. It is a correct classical statement in characteristic 0 and is stated by Tyomkin/CHT for arbitrary characteristic. It is a dependency, not a demonstrated gap.
issues.evidence: "The locus of integral plane curves of degree b and normalization genus g is locally closed and, when nonempty, has dimension 3b+g-1 [CHT2023]... This is the cited theorem with surface P^2 and line bundle O(b)."

coverage:
I read all LaTeX sections in full: introduction, models, polar, selector, adjugate, conductor, dimension, transfer and consequences.

Checked by computation:
- Selector/gadget permanent identity per_m(A(X)) = a0*G_D(X): brute-force Ryser permanents for (k,q) = (1,0), (2,0), (2,1) with random integer X and theta all match. Matrix sizes 11k-2q also match.
- Multihomogeneous coefficient bound against known tight determinantal families: smooth plane curves (n=r, d=3), generic P^3 sections of det_n (d=4) and quadric surfaces. In every case mu <= coefficient, and it is tight for d=2 and for the 2x2 quadric.

Checked by hand:
- Gradient-to-adjugate identity, and the H^1 vanishing argument showing that constant matrices surject onto H^0(J(k-1)).
- Complementary-monomial injectivity, which gives length Z >= T.
- Conductor contained in the evaluation ideal, and length(B/c) = length(R/B) (Gorenstein monogenic).
- delta formula and Severi bookkeeping: sum(3b_i+g_i-1) = k(k+3)/2 - delta.
- Row-adjugate subscheme: length N, uniqueness via the boundary frame at [1:0].
- Commuting-nilpotent bound for punctual Hilbert schemes, giving dim Hilb^N(C) <= N.
- Fiber count, giving dim Gamma <= k^2+k-T.
- Transfer from characteristic 2 to C: integral Proj family, upper semicontinuity of fiber dimension for a proper map over an integral base, and Euler's identity in characteristic 0.
- Bertini-type smooth-section incidence counts.
- Polar argument: persistence of simple zeros under coefficientwise approximation, kernel lift via Schur complement, homotopy-count lemma.
- All numerical constants: q >= k/4, T >= k^2/32, Delta >= k^2/64, d-1 >= k^2/200, k >= m/12, and 1728*3200 = 5,529,600.
